description:
FILED s473t5a (#1501 CHECK 1 round 2, 2026-09-13), found by corpus-diff while
fixing #1650.  PRE-EXISTING: identical on a `git archive 8c8fa4c0` extraction.

`Pl::Parser2::_blank_string_innards` blanks the innards of CL string literals
and line comments in the emitted text before the forward-declaration scans read
it, and its own comment says exactly why:

    an eval'd Perl source embedded as a string literal would otherwise defvar
    its own lexicals in the enclosing file -- proclaiming them special and
    silently breaking closures the eval builds (found by E3: eval.t #39) --
    and a sprintf "%x" format minted a phantom %x (task #66).

It stops doing that as soon as the file mentions `$|`.

THE MECHANISM.  perl's `$|` compiles to the pipe-quoted CL symbol `|$\||` --
the inner pipe is BACKSLASH-ESCAPED.  The blanker's pipe branch is

    if ($in_pipe) { $in_pipe = 0 if $ch eq '|'; next }

with no backslash handling, so the ESCAPED pipe closes the region; the very
next character, the real closing `|`, OPENS a new pipe region, and that one
runs to the next `|` anywhere in the file.  From there the blanker is one
region out of phase and string literals pass through raw.

MEASURED, on the base and on HEAD alike:

    $ cat strip3.pl
    $| = 1;
    my $code = 'my $phantomvar = 5; my @phantomary = (1,2); $phantomvar + @phantomary';
    my $r = eval $code;
    print "r=$r\n";

    $ ./pl2cl < strip3.pl | grep phantom
    (p-defcell $phantomvar (make-p-box nil))
    (p-defcell @phantomary (make-array 0 :adjustable t :fill-pointer 0))
    (p-my-= $code "my $phantomvar = 5; …")

Two globals declared for names that exist only inside a string.  In
perl-tests/sort.t the same desync reaches `(p-sprintf "%02x" …)`, which is how
#1650's first (wrong) name class minted a `%02x` -- so this bug is ALSO the
reason that mistake was visible at all.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE: honour a backslash inside the pipe branch, i.e.

    if ($in_pipe) {
      if ($ch eq '\\') { $i++; next }        # \| does not close the symbol
      $in_pipe = 0 if $ch eq '|';
      next;
    }

WHY IT IS NOT FIXED HERE: the blast radius is an EMISSION change across every
file that mentions `$|` and then has a string literal containing something
name-shaped -- i.e. most of the corpus -- and each differing file has to be
explained per the round rules.  MEASURE FIRST: apply the one line, run
`tools/corpus-diff.pl` and `tools/emission-ab.pl --shapes --list lib/**/*.pm`,
and expect the diffs to be PHANTOM DECLARATIONS DISAPPEARING (a removed
`p-defcell`/`defvar` line and nothing else).  Any other kind of diff means the
phantom was load-bearing somewhere and is a finding of its own.

HOW BAD IS IT TODAY: mostly benign since the #291 direction-D flip, by that
flip's own argument -- an ordinary global is a `p-defcell` symbol macro and a
`let` of the same name simply SHADOWS it, so a phantom cell is dead weight
rather than a poisoned binding.  The probe above runs correctly (`r=7`) on both
trees.  But the EXCEPTION partition still emits `defvar`, which DOES proclaim
the symbol special, so a phantom whose name lands in that partition is the
eval.t-#39 shape again; and "the blanker is a lie from the first `$|` onward"
is worth closing on its own.
subject: `$| = 1;` DESYNCS the free-global scan's string blanker -- `|$\||` closes the pipe region at the ESCAPED pipe, so every CL string literal after it is scanned as CODE and can mint a phantom global out of string DATA (the task-#66 / eval.t-#39 hazard, re-opened)
